title: LedgerMath data API, version 1: one month of a Series
description: v1/series/<id>/<yyyy-mm>.json: one month of one Series: every point of the Series' Runs that started that month (UTC, by the Run's start), under derivations, keyed <method name>_v<version> as in the Series' file, at the same paths and in the same words as LedgerMath's Method writes its Derivations; and series v1's entries of what differed between consecutive Runs, each filed under the month of the later Run. The Series' file (series_url) lists every month and holds each Method's summary, its definitions and the figures the points are read by. Each point also gives the sha256 of its Run file and the addresses of its evidence: the Run file (evidence) and its boot's summary (boot_summary). Numbers are exactly as the Derivation holds them; a duration is in nanoseconds of the Run's clock unless its field's name says otherwise. For a given layout (the layout of v1/index.json), a month file's bytes change only when (a) a Run that started in that month is added, (b) a boot summary that was missing arrives, (c) a Run arrives late, having started before a Run of the Series already in the files, in that month or an earlier one, or (d) a Method first applies to the Series; otherwise they do not change. These four are the only causes for a given layout: layout increases when LedgerMath changes how the files are written, and only then may a file's bytes change without one of them. A past month is therefore not immutable: each entry of the Series file's months gives its month file's sha256 and size in bytes, so a reader holding a copy can tell whether it is current, and fetches the file again only when the sha256 differs. A Series file and a month file fetched together can still be from different updates of the files: a cache may hold one of them from before the other changed, and an update that stopped halfway leaves them so until the next one. So a reader checks the sha256 of every month file it fetches against the one its Series file lists; on a mismatch, it fetches the Series file again, then the month file, and compares again; while they still differ, it uses neither, and tries again later. What each cause changes: (a) the month gains the Run's point, its pair entry and its count and span; (b) the point's boot_summary turns from null into the summary's address, and nothing else; (c) as (a), and in that month and every later one the points after the late Run may change only what depends on earlier Runs: their group, and requests v1's through and group_through_as_of_run (through's counts rise by exactly what the late Runs it pools add, and not at all when none of them is counted), and the pair entry of the Run right after it then comes from the late Run; (d) the Method's block appears, under its key, in every month file of the Series. Version 1 only ever gains fields: a field, once in a v1 file, keeps its name, its type and its meaning, and a reader ignores any field it does not know, which is why no object in this schema forbids members it does not list. A new Method, or a new version of one, is a new key beside the old ones. A change that would break a reader is published as v2, beside v1.

schema.description: What this file is, and which version of its shape.

index.description: The address of the table of contents, v1/index.json.

id.description: The Series' id: the first 12 hex digits of the sha256 of its key (benchmark, params, build, instance type, zone ID) as canonical JSON.

month.description: The month, yyyy-mm, UTC: every Run here started in it.

series_url.description: The address of the Series' file, v1/series/<id>.json, which lists every month of the Series.

benchmark.description: The benchmark's name, as its Runs give it.

params.description: The parameter set, as each Run was given it (LM_PARAM_*).

additionalProperties.description: One parameter's value, under the parameter's name, as each Run was given it.

build.description: The named build of the benchmark (static, dynamic).

instance_type.description: The EC2 instance type, as the provider names it.

availability_zone_id.description: The Availability Zone ID, as the provider names it.

runs.description: Runs of the Series that started this month, counted or not.

oldest_run_started_at.description: When the oldest of them started.

newest_run_started_at.description: When the newest of them started.

derivations.description: Each Method's points of the month, keyed <method name>_v<version> as in the Series' file. Method series v1 derives every Series; Method requests v1 only those whose samples are requests, and its key is absent from the others.

url.description: An address: an absolute URL starting http:// or https://.

time.description: UTC, to the nanosecond, as the Run records it.

point_path.description: The Run file's path, runs/<yyyy>/<mm>/<dd>/<id>.json: the name LedgerMath gives it, and its address under the API's base (evidence).

point_sha256.description: The sha256 of the Run file's bytes, in hex: what the Derivation cites.

point_boot_summary.description: The address of the summary of the boot the Run was part of, which accounts for every execution the boot was to run; null when LedgerMath held no summary of that boot when the file was made. A summary that arrives later turns it into the address, and is one of the four causes for which a month file changes.

point_group.description: The group its split facts put it in.

point_counted.description: Whether the Method counts the Run. A Run it does not count is shown, with why, and is left out of the Method's statistics.

point_failure.description: Why it is not counted, or null: the first 10 of its reasons, each cut to its first 500 characters, joined by "; ", then how many more there are.

method_series.description: The Method, by name and version: series, version 1.

series_v1_month.description: Method series, version 1, for the month's Runs.

points.description: Every Run of the Series that started this month, in time order.

differed.description: What differed between each pair of consecutive Runs of the Series whose later Run started this month, in order: the first entry's earlier Run is the previous month's last when the Series has one.

series_point.description: One Run on the Series' chart, with the sha256 of its Run file and the addresses of its evidence.

samples.description: Its counted samples, in stream order; empty when it is not counted.

sample.description: The sample's number in the stream.

ns.description: sample_ended.t minus sample_started.t, in nanoseconds of the Run's clock.

repetitions.description: How many repetitions of the measured work the sample holds, as its sample_started gives it.

time_per_repetition_ns.description: The median of its samples' ns_per_repetition: the Run's one number, 0 or more. Null when it is not counted; and null when it is infinite, past a double's range, which JSON cannot hold: when it is the mean of its two middle samples' ns_per_repetition and their sum overflows (both near the top of a double's range; no real clock comes near). Such a Run is still counted, and still among the Runs of its Series' and group's time_per_repetition_ns percentiles.

bytes_per_repetition.description: As the benchmark observed it, a positive number. Null when it is not counted, or when the benchmark observed no bytes per repetition.

bytes_per_second.description: bytes_per_repetition × 10^9 / time_per_repetition_ns. Null when either is null; and null when the quotient is infinite, past a double's range, which JSON cannot hold: chiefly a counted Run that observed a finite bytes per repetition above 0 and whose time per repetition is 0 (its median sample ended at the clock read it started at). Such a Run is still counted, and still among the Runs of its Series' and group's bytes_per_second percentiles.

differed.description: What differed between two consecutive Runs of the Series: the split facts whose values differ, and every section of the before-dump whose hash differs, split on or not.

facts.description: The split facts whose values differ between the two Runs, by name, in the order the Method's split_on lists them.

sections.description: Each section of the before-dump whose hash differs between the two Runs, split on or not, in order of name, with what its change did to the split.

effect.description: splits: its split fact differs; left out: it is split on but differs only in what is left out; not split on: no split fact is read from it.

keys.description: The section's top-level keys whose values differ; null when the section is not read, or is on one side only.

method_requests.description: The Method, by name and version: requests, version 1.

requests_v1_month.description: Method requests, version 1, for the month's Runs.

points.description: Every Run of the Series that started this month, in time order.

request_stats.description: One phase over a set of requests, in nanoseconds: the count of requests, the least and greatest time, and each percentile the count supports (null when it does not), with how many requests are ranked at or above each one reported.

count.description: How many requests the figures are of: those of the set that succeeded and had this phase.

min.description: The least of their times, in nanoseconds, exactly.

max.description: The greatest of their times, in nanoseconds, exactly.

p50.description: The 50th percentile of their times, in nanoseconds; null when count is under 2, too few to support it. In one Run's own statistics, interpolated between its sorted times; in pooled statistics, read from the summed histogram, within 1/128 of the exact percentile.

p90.description: The 90th percentile of their times, in nanoseconds; null when count is under 10, too few to support it. In one Run's own statistics, interpolated between its sorted times; in pooled statistics, read from the summed histogram, within 1/128 of the exact percentile.

p95.description: The 95th percentile of their times, in nanoseconds; null when count is under 20, too few to support it. In one Run's own statistics, interpolated between its sorted times; in pooled statistics, read from the summed histogram, within 1/128 of the exact percentile.

p99.description: The 99th percentile of their times, in nanoseconds; null when count is under 100, too few to support it. In one Run's own statistics, interpolated between its sorted times; in pooled statistics, read from the summed histogram, within 1/128 of the exact percentile.

p99.9.description: The 99.9th percentile of their times, in nanoseconds; null when count is under 1000, too few to support it. In one Run's own statistics, interpolated between its sorted times; in pooled statistics, read from the summed histogram, within 1/128 of the exact percentile.

at_or_above.description: For each percentile reported, how many requests are ranked at or above it (ties counted by rank).

p50.description: How many requests are ranked at or above the 50th percentile; absent when it is not reported.

p90.description: How many requests are ranked at or above the 90th percentile; absent when it is not reported.

p95.description: How many requests are ranked at or above the 95th percentile; absent when it is not reported.

p99.description: How many requests are ranked at or above the 99th percentile; absent when it is not reported.

p99.9.description: How many requests are ranked at or above the 99.9th percentile; absent when it is not reported.

phase_stats.description: Each phase's statistics, by phase; a phase no request had is absent (dns, connect and tls over a kept connection).

failure_count.description: Failures of one kind: where (phase), what kind, and how many. Under failures they are requests that failed; under setups_failed they are setups of a kept connection that failed outside any sample, whose phase and kind are their connection_failed event's phase and error.

phase.description: For a request that failed: record when the binary withheld one of its lines (a withheld certificate line, its withheld_event the string certificate, is set aside first, like a certificate event, and is no failure); otherwise request_failed.phase, or response for a complete response whose status is not 2xx. For a setup of a kept connection that failed (setups_failed): the phase its connection_failed event gives.

kind.description: For a request that failed: for record, from the first withheld line in stream order that is not a certificate's, line_withheld_<event> when it names the event it replaced as a word of a-z, 0-9 and _ starting with a letter, and line_withheld when it does not; otherwise request_failed.error, or status_<code>. For a setup of a kept connection that failed (setups_failed): the error its connection_failed event gives.

count.description: How many failed in that phase with that kind of failure, 1 or more.

failures.description: Failures counted by where and what kind: each entry gives a phase, a kind of failure, and how many failed with both.

pool_summary.description: The pooled figures as they stood through one Run: the counted Runs that started at or before it. What a citation of an earlier moment is checked against.

runs.description: How many counted Runs it pools.

requests.description: How many succeeded requests it pools.

failed.description: How many of its counted requests failed, never timed.

failures.description: Its failed requests, by where and what kind of failure, with how many.

requests_point.description: One Run of the Series, with the sha256 of its Run file and the addresses of its evidence.

exit_code.description: The binary's exit code, or null when a signal ended it.

counted_requests.description: Counted samples in its stream (counted requests); null when there was none to count.

succeeded.description: Of the counted requests, those that succeeded; 0 for a Run not counted.

failed.description: Of the counted requests, those that failed; 0 for a Run not counted.

phases.description: Its own succeeded requests' statistics per phase, exactly; empty for a Run not counted or one whose every request failed.

failures.description: Its counted requests that failed, by where and what kind of failure, with how many; empty for a Run not counted.

setups_failed.description: Its setups of a kept connection that failed outside any sample, by where and what kind of failure, with how many; empty for a Run not counted.

warmup_failure.description: How the warmup request failed, or null.

phase.description: Where the warmup request failed, read as a counted request's failure is: its certificate events, and a withheld certificate line (its withheld_event the string certificate), are set aside first; then it is record when the binary withheld any other of its lines; otherwise request_failed.phase, or response for a complete response whose status is not 2xx.

kind.description: What kind of failure, read in the same order: for record, line_withheld_<event> from the first withheld line in stream order that is not a certificate's, when it names the event it replaced as a word of a-z, 0-9 and _ starting with a letter, and line_withheld when it does not; otherwise request_failed.error, or status_<code>.

through.description: The Series' pooled figures through this Run; null before its first counted Run.

group_through_as_of_run.description: Its group's pooled figures through this Run (the counted Runs of its group that started at or before it), as they stood through this Run: a Run that started later never changes it, as such a Run never changes through (a Run that started earlier and arrives late can change both: cause (c) of when a month file changes). It is null for two reasons: the Series had had Runs of one group only, up to and including this Run; or its group had had no counted Run by this Run (a group whose first Run is not counted, say), even when through, which pools every group, has figures. requests v1's Derivation has a field group_through that differs from it in one case only: in a Series that later has more than one group, the Derivation gives each point before the Series' first Run of a group other than the first its group's figures, which are then the Series' own, its through. To recover the Derivation's group_through, take through for exactly those points: the points before the first point whose group differs from the first point's, in a Series whose requests_v1 groups number more than one (the Series file's). Take this field as it is for every other point. Never substitute through for a null otherwise: a null on a point of a group with no counted Run yet stands beside a through that holds other groups' figures.
